newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest stocks up, second tier in focus.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest stocks up, second tier in focus.

text.p: Heavy demand, especially from foreigners, led most Bucharest stocks to higher closing quotes on Tuesday. The biggest gains were posted on the second tier.
Twenty-five stocks, including 23 on the second tier, closed firmer, 11 fell and five were flat. Four companies had no trade and two were suspended.
"We had average price rises of up to 44 percent in lower- tier stocks," a broker said. "Turnover on this tier also grew, doubling to more than four billion lei."
Traders forecast further gains for second tier stocks throughout the week.
Overall turnover was 16.5 billion lei, some four billion down from Monday. Volume thinned to 3.3 million shares from 3.7 million.
Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, rose by 2.63, 2.67 and 2.6 percent respectively from Monday.

Carbide maker Carbid-Fox and Armatura industrial fittings maker were the most heavily traded second- tier listings. They both firmed at close, with Carbid adding 250 lei to 7,250 and Armatura gaining 400 lei to 7,400.
"Higher bids are offered on the second tier to prod shareholders to throw larger packages," said a trader.
The first tier, which is more liquid, still dominated trading in volume and turnover levels. Some 2.4 million shares were traded in this section on turnover of 12.2 billion lei.
But four of the eight high-caps ended lower and only two firmed under buying pressure towards the end of the session.

Sofert fertiliser maker closed 1,600 lei stronger at 41,100. Vehicle part maker Compa gained 150 lei to 3,050. Oltchim chemical plant, which had the highest traded volume in this section, ended flat at 5,200.
